# Shaping learning performance through artificial intelligence capability: Do cognitive competence, self-efficacy, creativity, and self-learning 

# competence mediate the relationship?

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

### Meghna Thakur [a,](#international-journal-of-educational-development) Akansha Chauhan [b,](#international-journal-of-educational-development) Vishal Sharma [a,\*](#international-journal-of-educational-development)

a _Himachal Pradesh University Business School, Himachal Pradesh University, Shimla, India_ b _Department of Commerce, Himachal Pradesh University, Shimla, India_

## ARTICLE INFO ABSTRACT

### _Keywords:_ Over the last few years, discussion among academicians and policymakers on the role of artificial intelligence 

Artificial intelligence capability (AI) technologies in shaping students’ learning performance (LP) has significantly increased. Hence, the study Learning performance aims to examine the influence of artificial intelligence capability (AIC) on LP. Additionally, the study investigates Cognitive competence

the mediating role of cognitive competence (CC), self-efficacy (SE), creativity (CR), and self-learning competence 

Self-efficacy Creativity and self -learning competence (SLC) in the relationship between AIC and LP. A survey method was employed to collect primary data from 416 

students of higher education in the Delhi-NCR region. Furthermore, partial least square structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the study’s hypotheses. The study reveals that SLC has a strongest impact on LP, followed by CC, AIC, SE, and CR. Furthermore, the study’s outcomes delineate that CC, SE, CR, and SLC establish complementary partial mediation in a relationship between AIC and LP. The study offers valuable insights to students, educators, higher education institutions, and policymakers and enhances their knowledge base on the determinants of students’ LP. Additionally, the study suggests policy interventions for various stakeholders to improve students’ LP. The study is an inaugural attempt to investigate the influence of AIC on higher education students’ LP in an emerging economy India. Moreover, the study is the first of its kind to 

investigate the impact of AIC on LP in the presence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC.

However, the adoption of AI-based technologies in educational set- tings is not uniform since their essentiality and effectiveness vary based on different disciplines such as arts, engineering, and medicine. For instance, in the arts discipline, students face challenges such as devel- oping creative thinking and transforming imaginative ideas into several artifacts. In this regard, AI tools such as generative art platforms can assist arts students in fostering creativity and provide immediate feed- back and stylistic suggestions ([Cetinic and She, 2022)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Moreover, in disciplines like engineering, where students continually deal with complex and open-ended technical problems, students need to adopt different and innovative learning strategies. In the context of the engi- neering discipline, AI-based educational technologies can provide automated tutoring systems, real-time performance tracking, and design simulation, which can enhance students’ self-efficacy and their learning performance (Martínez-Fernandez ´ et al., 2022). Furthermore, in the medical discipline, students are expected to acquire a vast body of knowledge, understand clinical trials, and understand the functioning of the human body in minute detail, which poses significant hurdles in learning (Tran et al., 2019). Hence, AI-enabled technologies can be utilized in interpreting complex medical images of the human body and ensure learning through virtual practical labs. Ergo, it becomes imper- ative for students in diverse disciplines to build AIC to enhance their learning. Due to the rising relevance of AI integration in education and an urgent need to develop AI-based capabilities among students, re- searchers initiated a focus to investigate the role of AIC in shaping stu- dents learning performance (LP) (e.g., Wang et al., 2022). Prior studies advocate the integral role of students’ engagement with AI in their learning process to enhance their academic performance. However, there is scant empirical evidence on the relationship between students’ AIC and their LP in education literature. Moreover, Liu and Nesbit (2023) expound on the essentiality of students’ ability to comprehend, process, and utilize information, known as cognitive competence (CC), which plays a vital role in enhancing their LP. Additionally, researchers state that the development of skills is not sufficient; a positive belief in the ability to apply knowledge and skills, known as self-efficacy (SE), is paramount to improving students’ LP (Zhao et al., 2019). Furthermore, Shahzad et al. (2024) emphasize the importance of creativity (CR) in attaining the desired LP. Apart from these capabilities, researchers advocate that students’ ability to learn by themselves, known as self-learning competence (SLC), is an interesting phenomenon and of utmost importance in the world of rapid technological advancements in enhancing students’ performance (e.g., Rashid and Asghar, 2016; Kim et al., 2022).

Mikalef and Gupta (2021), [Celik (2023),](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) and Wang et al. (2023) advocate that students’ AIC is behind the development of capabilities such as CC, SE, CR, and SLC. Nevertheless, due to the substantial in- fluence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC, no real attempt has been made to empirically examine how students’ AIC influences their LP in the pres- ence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC. Accordingly, our study is the first study of its kind to provide empirical evidence on how the relationship between AIC and LP changes in the presence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC with the help of the following research questions (RQs): 

**RQ1**. Does AIC influence students’ LP?

**RQ2**. Do CC, SE, CR, and SLC mediate the relationship between AIC and LP?

Against the above-mentioned background, the current study sub- stantially contributes to theory and practice. This study aims to fill the gap in the limited understanding of AIC at the student level. The study expounds on how an individual can refine their cognitive and creative skills by integrating AI tools meaningfully into their learning journey. AIC aims to build knowledge of an individual and provide directions to their learning journey; however, limited understanding of appropriate 

adoption of AI and the sudden boom in the number of AI tools require studies that examine how developing AIC can influence LP ([Dalgıç et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Although few studies investigate the role of AIC in shaping stu- dents’ LP (e.g., Wang et al., 2023), this study extends the literature by investigating the influence of AIC on students’ LP in higher education in emerging economy India. India is an emerging economy that faces sig- nificant challenges in terms of access to quality education, teacher shortage, and skill gaps among the young generation; hence, it requires technological integration in education to address these issues (Pillai et al., 2023). Remarkably, India has been a pioneer in technological adoption; several government initiatives, like Digital India and National Education Policy, have promoted AI-based education (Ziesche et al., 2022). The country’s socio-economic landscape, linguistic diversity, large student population, and emerging EdTech space make the country an ideal place to examine the role of AIC on students’ LP. Moreover, the study is an inaugural attempt to empirically examine the mediating role of CC, SE, CR, and SLC in a relationship between AIC and LP, enriching the education literature. Moreover, the study enhances the knowledge base of educators, students, higher education institutions, and policy- makers on determinants of LP in contemporary society and suggests practical policy interventions. This would assist in policymaking and attaining higher students’ LP and their holistic development. The remaining sections are as follows: Section two presents theo- retical underpinning and hypotheses development; Section three en- compasses research methodology; Section four entails data analysis and interpretation; Section five discusses the results; Section five mentions theoretical and practical implications; and Section seven concludes the study, acknowledge the shortcomings, and proposes future research agenda.

## 2. Theoretical underpinnings and hypotheses development

With the development of knowledge-based societies, every segment is witnessing continuous technological upgradation, and even the edu- cation sector is not isolated from this phenomenon ([Algerafi et al., 2023)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Furthermore, due to the emergence of artificial neural networks and deep learning, AI has penetrated the educational environment deeply (Grzybowski et al., 2024). AI has emerged as an imperative tool since it offers personalized learning experiences, solves complex prob- lems, and delivers real-time feedback, thus providing a more inclusive and effective learning environment ([Chandra et al., 2022)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Hence, the role of AI in education and enhancing learning performance has garnered significant attention among academic researchers and policy- makers (Mikalef and Gupta, 2021; Celik, 2023). Moreover, prior studies advocate that students’ belief in their learning abilities, cognitive competence, indulgence in creating tasks, and self-learning are crucial to harness the potential of AI in learning (Hernandez-Orallo, 2016´ ). Cor- ollary, to rationalize this phenomenon, the present study uses the resource-based view theory ([Barney, 2001)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-), which emphasizes the role of intangible resources, tangible resources, and dynamic capabilities in improving individual and organizational performance. Moreover, we utilize self-efficacy theory ([Bandura and Adams, 1977)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-), which empha- sizes the role of perseverance, human cognition, action, motivation, and emotion to achieve desired outcomes and actively shape their environ- ment rather than being a passive reactor. Moreover, to address the technological aspect in the current study, we also utilize technological self-efficacy theory conceptualized by [Compeau and Higgins (1995).](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) This theory deals with learners’ confidence in their ability to engage with digital tools and capture learners’ confidence in a technology-rich environment or AI-embedded tools. Ergo, the present study takes into consideration AIC as an independent variable based on these theories and pertinent literature (Wang et al., 2022; Shahzad et al., 2024b; Mikalef and Gupta, 2021), while LP is the dependent variable. However, the primary emphasis of this research is to investigate the mediating role of CC, SE, CR, and SLC between AIC and LP, as shown in [Fig. 1.](#21-aic-and-lp-ual-to-focus-on-essential-operations-which-amplifies-academic) The main guiding idea behind using CC, SE, CR and SLC s mediators was their

### _2.5._ _AIC and SLC_

SLC refers to the ability of an individual to acquire knowledge and skills on their own and align the learning objective to their personal goals or perceived demands accordingly (Jia et al., 2024). Prior studies advocate that AIC has a significant association with students’ ability to learn at their own pace (e.g., Huang, 2021; Jia and Tu, 2024). Ifenthaler et al. (2024) state that AIC enhances SLC by fostering inclusive, inte- grated, and practical educational experiences. Additionally, AIC in- stigates goal setting, self-monitoring resourcefulness, time management, self-assessment motivation, and emotional support with the help of an emotionally intelligent tutoring system that improves SLC (Rapp et al., 2021). AI tools aid self-learning by providing customized support and resources, enabling students to take changes in their learning journey (Jia and Tu, 2024). Moreover, Huang (2021) concludes that AIC en- hances the critical thinking of learners, which assists them in handling their learning without other human intervention, ultimately enhancing SLC (Huang, 2021b). However, Gupta and Bhaskar (2020) and Jia and Tu (2024) state that although students’ AIC enhances their SLC in the short term, lack of teachers’ involvement and insufficient planning may also hinder SLC in the long term. Moreover, overdependency on AI can impede students' SLC over time. Xu and Babaian (2021) state that stu- dents often accept AI-generated answers without any questions, which leads to diminished critical thinking and lowers SLC. In addition, Zhai and Wibowo, 2024 conclude that overreliance on AI-generated context may decrease the competencies that students require for self-regulated learning, ultimately affecting the SLC negatively. 

**H5:**. AIC significantly influences students’ SLC.

### _2.6._ _CC and LP_

Academic literature advocates that CC is essential for improving LP since it comprises fundamental skills such as problem-solving, attention, and memory (e.g., Jia and Tu,2024; [Celik et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Furthermore, Liu and Nesbit (2023) state that internally motivated students and those involved in cognitive tasks reflect higher academic performance. Peng et al. (2022) conclude that CC significantly improves students’ LP since it includes cognitive skills that promote sustained attention, meta- cognitive skills, working memory, and processing speed. Additionally, Zhao et al. (2019) and Wang and Chuang (2023) observe that cognitive skills are essential for improving students’ LP as they enable students to adapt to evolving learning environments and solve complex problems. [Demetriou et al. (2020)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) argue that certain cognitive functions, such as attention control and flexibility, generally decline with age, lowering LP. 

**H6:**. CC significantly influences students’ LP.

### _2.7._ _SE and LP_

Prior research shows a significant relationship between SE and LP (Shahzad et al., 2024; Wang and Chuang, 2023). Higher SE improves students’ motivation and persistence, leading to higher LP (e.g., Zhao et al., 2019). Jia et al. (2024) state that students with higher SE tend to reflect higher academic engagement with their studies, which results in improved LP. Additionally, Jiang and Jiang (2024) conclude that SE enables students to manage their emotions more appropriately during learning, which enhances their skills and LP. Moreover, Honicke et al. (2023) emphasize that when students believe positively in their abilities, they are more likely to focus on self-directed learning, ultimately improving their LP. Zhao et al. (2019) reveal that SE enhances students’ academic outcomes since students with high SE are open to constructive 

feedback and self-reflection. Ergo, we propose the study’s seventh hypothesis: 

**H7:**. SE significantly influences students’ LP.

### _2.8._ _CR and LP_

Academic literature highlights the significant association between CR and LP (e.g., Jia et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2023). According to Yan et al. (2022), CR significantly improves students' LP through the visual organization of thoughts and allows them to explore multiple ideas. Furthermore, Jin et al. (2022) state that CR fosters LP by developing critical skills and enhancing innovative thinking and motivation. Moreover, Shahzad et al. (2024) conclude that CR encourages students to engage cognitively by exploring the concepts more deeply, leading to novel ideas and solutions, ultimately enhancing the student's LP. Furthermore ([Esiyok et al. (2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) reveals that students with higher CR tend to go beyond root learning and traditional learning patterns and are more likely to engage in learning new things which enhance their LP. 

**H8:**. CR significantly influences’ students’ LP.

### _2.9._ _SLC and LP_

Academic literature highlights that when students engage in self- learning tasks, it significantly enhances their LP (e.g., Hardy et al., 2016; chang et al., 2023; Honicke et al., 2023). SLC enables students to generate novel ideas that foster their learning and enhance performance (Sahoo et al., 2023). Moreover, Jin et al. (2022) state that SLC leads to deeper understanding, better engagement, and strong problem-solving skills and enables students to learn effectively along with fulfilling other essential commitments, which leads to higher LP (Hargreaves et al., 2023). Individuals with high SLC acknowledge their learning needs and conveniently utilize learning resources and time, improving LP (chang et al., 2023). Furthermore, Rashid and Asghar (2016) state that SLC assists individuals to take control of their learning and identify the existing learning gaps which enable them to tailor their strategy according to their needs, further enhancing their LP. 

**H9:**. SLC significantly influences students’ LP.

### _2.10._ _CC, SE, CR, SLC as mediators_

Researchers in the past highlight the CC, SE, CR, and SLC connection with AIC (e.g., Mikalef and Gupta, 2021; [Celik, 2023;](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) Wang and Chuang, 2023; Shahzad et al., 2024). Scholars in these studies assert that AIC assists learners in making informed decisions about their learning pro- cess and solves their learning problems, which develops cognitive abil- ities (e.g., Zhao et al., 2019; Rapp et al., 2021). The development of cognitive abilities facilitates students’ learning and enhances their LP (Liu and Nesbit, 2023). AIC gives an individual edge by building competence to use AI tools efficiently, which in turn instills deeper thinking and problem-solving capability, allowing an individual to explore and experiment with numerous creative spaces, which further boost their CR in the longer run (Parker et al., 2023). Additionally, re- searchers conclude that when students become proficient in utilizing AI in their learning process, it offers them innovative tools to master their domain, which enhances their belief in learning capabilities ([Adam et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2022)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) This belief in their learning capabilities makes learning easier that leads to higher LP. Moreover, Xiao and Hew (2024) and Shahzad et al. (2024) highlight that students with high AIC tend to be more creative in their studies and show better cognitive abilities in solving complex problems, ultimately improving their LP. AI tools provide personalized feedback and learning analytics, encouraging autonomy and self-regulation. In addition, [Esiyok et al. (2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) demon- strate that students who show high SLC learn at their own pace and personalize their learning experience as per their needs, which enhances 

their LP. In this context, Ifenthaler et al. (2024) reveal that students with high AIC are in a better position to plan their studies and personalize their learning process to ensure better academic performance. Hence, based on the above discussion, we propose the following hypotheses: 

**H10**. **-**CC mediates the relationship between AIC and LP

**H11**. **-** SE, mediates the relationship between AIC and LP.

**H12**. **-** CR mediates the relationship between AIC and LP.

**H13**. - SLC mediates the relationship between AIC and LP.

## 3. Research methodology

### _3.1._ _Evaluation framework_

Prior studies advocate that Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the power to revolutionize higher education other than any technological devel- opment ([Bates et al., 2020)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) since it focuses on personalized learning based on learners’ needs (Huang et al., 2021). Building AI-related ca- pabilities among students in higher education is paramount as it en- hances their learning abilities and enables them to become job-ready (Rahiman and Kodikal, 2023). Corollary, this study attempts to examine the impact of AIC on students’ LP in the presence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC in higher education in India. To accomplish the study’s objectives, the measurement scale of 26 items is developed following the thorough examination of relevant literature (e.g., [Demetriou et al., 2019;](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) Honicke et al., 2023; Shahzad et al., 2024; [Esiyok et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). A panel of six experts was formed to validate these items, and an online meeting was organized with them. The experts include three academicians working in the field of education and three industry professionals with experi- ence in the field of AI. Moreover, to ensure the reliability and validity of questionnaire we conducted the pilot testing of the instrument on 100 students in higher education and analyzed the reliability and validity. After the expert validation and pilot testing, we gather the data employing a 5-point Likert scale with options ranging from “Strongly Disagree” to “Strongly Agree.” Prior studies in the domain have also employed a 5-point Likert scale to investigate variables of similar nature (e.g., [Chatterjee and Bhattacharjee, 2020;](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) Habibi et al., 2023; Ivanov et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2022).

### _3.2._ _Designing of questionnaire_

A structured questionnaire was framed to collect primary data from higher education students. The questionnaire contains the caption, “This survey aims to conduct an empirical study on how artificial intelligence capability, cognitive competence, self-efficacy, creativity and self- learning competence impact the learning performance of the students in higher education.” The questionnaire is separated into two parts. The first part integrates the four questions related to demographic infor- mation, namely, gender, age, qualification, and streams. The second part comprises the items related to various constructs of the study, namely AIC, CC, SE, CR, SLC, and LP. AIC is adopted from Mikalef and Gupta (2021), CC is adopted from [Celik (2023),](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) SE is adopted from Wang and Chuang (2023), CR is adopted from Shahzad et al. (2024), SLC is adopted from [Esiyok et al. (2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) and LP is adopted from McGill and Klobas (2008).

### _3.3._ _Data collection_

The study obtains primary data from Indian higher education stu- dents in the Delhi NCR region. Delhi NCR is an education hub in India, comprised of several reputed higher education institutions, including state universities, central universities, and institutes of national impor- tance (Kumar et al., 2020; Srivastava and Dhamija, 2022). We employ a purposive sampling technique to collect data from respondents. Purpo- sive sampling is a non-probability sampling used when data has to be 

collected based on a specific attribute (higher education students in the present context) (Sabharwal et al., 2023). We applied the [Cochran (1963)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) formula to ascertain the accurate sample size, which is appro- priate when the population is large and infinite. The study employed the inclusion and exclusion criteria to meet the objectives of the research and to ensure the data were gathered appropriately (Shahzad et al., 2024). The inclusion criteria for the study focused on university students who were currently enrolled in higher education institutions that incorporate AI-based technologies into their teaching and learning process. Further, only those students were considered who had experi- ence with AI-based tools in their studies. Additionally, only individuals who were 18 and above and capable of understanding the questionnaire were included in the study. Students were excluded from the study if they had no access to AI-based courses, were from non-academic courses without AI integration, or were under 18 years of age. Moreover, we informed the participants about the study’s objectives and obtained their voluntary consent. In addition, their responses were kept anony- mous and confidential, and no personal information was included in the data to ensure the ethical guidelines were followed. Thus, 2550 students in higher education of different ages, institutions, and courses corpus were reached out physically and electronically (via email, WhatsApp web, and telegram) to fill out the final questionnaire from May 2024 to October 2024. Several personal and telephonic interviews were con- ducted with students to ensure their comprehensibility of the ques- tionnaire. A total of 468 respondents answered positively to the questionnaire, of which 52 responses were incomplete. Hence, we removed them from the final analysis. The remaining 416 questionnaires were considered for the final analysis, indicating a response rate of 16.31%. Studies in the domain have also utilized approximately similar sample sizes (e.g., [Chan and Hu, 2023;](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-) Sharma et al., 2024).

### _3.4._ _Analytical approach_

The present study employs partial least square structure equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to attain the study’s objectives. PLS-SEM is a commonly used method for investigating the complex model encom- passing multiple mediating relationships and measuring the results’ predictive quality (Hair et al., 2018). The current study also involves examining intricate models. It analyzes the influence of AIC on LP with the mediating role of CC, SE, CR, and SLC. Moreover, this approach is more effective than the maximum likelihood method and is employed in expanding an existing theory (Jain et al., 2023). The current study also expands the resource-based view theory and self-efficacy theory in the field of education. Corollary, the current adopts PLS-SEM as an analyt- ical approach. Moreover, the study prefers the use of PLS-SEM over the Covariance-based SEM (CB-SEM), since Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test reveals that the dataset utilized in the current study is not normally distributed. PLS-SEM does not assume the normality of the data, which makes it an appropriate analytical approach for analyzing non-normal data, as is the case in the current study (Hair et al., 2018). Similar studies in the past have also employed PLS-SEM to test the study’s hy- potheses (e.g., Sabharwal et al., 2023; Sharma et al., 2024).

### _3.5._ _Participants description_

The sample consists male respondents (i.e., 52%) whereas female responses comprise of 48%. This sample is similar with (Raman et al., 2024) where male constituted about (51.39%) of the sample. Further- more, the findings reveal that, the age group of 20–25 years comprised the vast majority of students (42%) in the study. This distribution is consistent with the study of Sabharwal et al. (2023). Along with that, 38% of students were graduates, 53% were postgraduates and 9% were doctorates which is similar with (Malik et al., 2021) who reports that most of the respondents were post-graduates. The majority of the re- spondents (36%) and (30%) belongs to the arts and commerce back- ground, the same results as reported in the research of ([Ali et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-).

### _4.4._ _Importance performance map analysis (IPMA)_

The present study employs the importance-performance matrix, a reliable method to strengthen the study’s results (Ringle and Sarstedt, 2016). IPMA reveals the most critical factor that drives the students’ LP. IPMA presents a strong total effect on the target construct (LP In the present context) and recognizes the most critical variable in the study. IPMA is an appropriate method in the present study since it involves multiple mediators, and the study’s model has complex meditating ef- fects (Direct effects + indirect effects = total effect). [Table 8](#44-importance-performance-map-analysis-ipma) presents the total effect of AIC, CC, SE, CR, and SLC on LP for unstandardized effect, which is similar to unstandardized weights of ordinary least square regression modeling (Hair et al., 2010). The performance of LP is ob- tained as 64.374

After confirming that all the necessary conditions are met, we obtain the IPMA map by calculating the mean values of importance and performance of exogenous con- structs. Fig. 3 reveals that AIC has relatively low performance of 57.892 compared to the average performance of other constructs. However, with the importance of 0.588. it shows high importance compared to other predictors. Hence, an increase in one unit of AIC performance from 57.892 to 58.892 would increase the performance of LP by 0.588 from 64.374 to 64.962. Hence, AIC requires managerial and policymakers’ attention to improve students’ LP in higher education.

## 5. Discussion

The current study attempts to examine how artificial intelligence capability (AIC), cognitive competence (CC), self-efficacy (SE), crea- tivity (CR), and self-learning competence (SLC) affect the learning per- formance (LP) of students in higher education. Moreover, the study examines the mediating role of CC, SE, CR, and SLC in a relationship between AIC and LP. The study’s outcomes reveal that all five variables investigated in the study have a considerable effect on LP, with SLC having the strongest influence, followed by CC, AIC, SE, and CR in their 

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Fig. 3.** IPMA map. **Source:** 

respective orders. The positive relationship between SLC and LP makes sense as students with high SLC feel responsible for their education and ensure continuous learning which improves their LP. These findings are consistent with previous research studies (e.g., Gupta and Bhaskar, 2020; Mikalef and Gupta, 2021; Jia and Tu, 2024). Moreover, the study’s outcomes disclose that students with high CC are more likely to select appropriate study material and focus only on material activities, improving their decision-making and LP. These results align with pre- vious studies (e.g., Wingstrom ¨ et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2019). The study’s outcomes reveal that AIC significantly and positively influences students’ LP. AI-competent students have shown better LP since AIC allows learners to access the much-needed technological resources for their learning, build skills, assist in time management, and identify learning gaps, which enhance their LP. Moreover, AIC enables students to utilize gamification techniques, which enhance their engagement in studies and improve LP ([Almheiri et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship in India has also started the Na- tional Program on Artificial Intelligence Skilling Framework to equip individuals with AI capabilities (UGC, 2023). These findings support the prior studies (e.g., Peng et al., 2022; Villa et al. 2023).

Furthermore, the study reports a positive and significant relationship between SE and LP. The plausible rationale behind this association is that students who believe positively in their capabilities tend to effi- ciently and effectively deal with study-related challenges that enhance their perseverance and LP (Peng et al.,2022). Moreover, the study re- ports that CR significantly influences LP. The rationale behind these findings is that CR helps students to go beyond rote memorization and traditional learning patterns, which fuel an individual’s motivation and perseverance, putting students in a position to learn better. The study’s results support the findings of (e.g., Wingstrom et al., 2022¨ ; Jia et al., 2024). The present study’s result also indicates that AIC significantly affects the CC, SE, CR, and SLC of students. AIC augments human abil- ities and enables individuals to dive deep into cognition, fostering cognitive competence ([Dong et al., 2024; McGill and Klobas, 2008)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). The study’s results disclose that AIC improves students’ SE by providing them access to technological educational resources such as simulations and interactive platforms, thereby increasing their confidence in their 

Authors’ compilation.

capabilities. Moreover, AIC augments students’ skills in generating ideas, solving complex problems, and providing diverse perspectives on a study topic, fostering their creativity. Additionally, the study reveals that AIC significantly enhances SLC since AIC enables students to take charge of their learning, foster resilience, and acquire lifelong learning habits, thereby enhancing SLC (Jia et al., 2024). These findings are consistent with previous studies (e.g., Rapp et al., 2021; Novikova et al., 2022; Jia et al., 2024)

Additionally, the present study examines the mediating effect of CC, SE, CR, and SLC in the relationship between AIC and LP. The study re- veals that AIC significantly influences LP in the presence of CC. The plausible reason for this association is that AIC enables students to enhance their cognitive processes like information processing, synthesis, and evaluation, ultimately improving academic learning performance ([Celik, 2023)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Additionally, the study expounds on the significant and positive mediating effect of SE in a relationship between AIC and LP. Students who show high skills in utilizing AI-based technologies in their learning tend to receive personalized guidance and feedback, which improves their positive belief in their skills, thus leading to higher LP (Marcus and Teuwen, 2024). Moreover, the study reports that AIC in- fluences LP profoundly and positively in the presence of CR since AIC fosters divergent and out-of-the-box thinking, which assists them in exploring creative ways of study, thereby enhancing their LP. Further- more, the study reveals that SLC significantly changes the relationship between AIC and LP. The rationale behind this association is that stu- dents with high AIC are exposed to personalized learning experience which enables them to plan their education according to their needs, enhancing their engagement and improving their confidence in man- aging their learning on their own (Miracchi, 2019). This engagement in the learning process and confidence in managing the learning results in higher LP. Although the indirect effect of AIC on LP in the presence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC is significant, it is less than the direct effect but still positive. The reasoning behind this finding is that AIC significantly re- duces students' emotional and cognitive loads by offering personalized and ready-made study solutions, which diminishes the role of other capabilities like CC, SE, CR, and SLC. However, CC, SE, CR, and SLC still show complementary partial mediation between AIC and LP; these 

capabilities are essential and cannot be ignored in the long term in enhancing the students’ LP (Kim et al., 2022; Algerafi et al. 2023). The current study sheds light on the impact of AIC on LP through CC, CR, SE, and SLC in a generalized way. However, it is imperative to recognize the differences among students across disciplines that shape the influence of AIC on LP. For instance, students in the arts and hu- manities may utilize AI tools to generate creative ideas, develop critical thinking, and analyze historical incidents in present scenarios, which can significantly enhance their LP. Moreover, developing AIC among engineering students may assist them in developing simulation, error- free coding, and performing computational thinking tasks, which im- proves their LP. Meanwhile, improved AIC among medical students makes them more capable of dealing with complex medical conditions and understanding human body issues, which can substantially contribute to their learning. Furthermore, high AIC may assist com- merce students in building financial models, analyzing complex finan- cial data, and performing business analytics efficiently, which can improve their LP in the long run.

## 6. Implications

### _6.1._ _Theoretical implications_

Over the last few years, significant technological advancements have paved the way for integrating AI-based technologies into students’ learning process (Shahzad et al., 2024). Educational institutions worldwide have started incorporating AI-powered tools in their teaching and learning practices, especially chatbots, intelligent tutoring, and automated grading systems (Rahiman and Kodikal, 2023). Conse- quently, the study extends theoretical contribution in the field of AI and education and related theories, such as resource-based view theory, self-efficacy theory, and technological self-efficacy theory as well by empirically investigating the influence of AIC on LP by integrating four mediators, namely CC, SE, CR, and SLC. The study’s results highlight the importance of AIC in developing capabilities such as CC, SE, CR, and SLC, which ultimately improves the students’ LP, confirming the resource-based view, self-efficacy. To the authors’ best knowledge, studies in the past have directly examined the influence of AIC on LP. The study is an inaugural attempt to provide empirical evidence on the mediating role of CC, SE, CR, and SLC in a relationship between AIC and LP.

### _6.2._ _Practical implications_

The study has practical implications for students, educators, man- agement of educational institutions, and policymakers. The study en- hances students’ knowledge base on determining their LP, which will help them plan their studies accordingly. We encourage students to enroll in online courses related to AI and their domain to enhance their LP and build future ready skills. Moreover, the study is beneficial to educators and the management of educational institutions since it assists them in comprehending the determinants of students’ LP. We suggest educators provide tutorials and demonstrations in the classroom to students on how to utilize AI-based technologies in the learning process. Moreover, educators can assign independent and collaborative projects to students to enhance their SE and SLC to improve their academic performance. Furthermore, educators can organize AI hackathons and competitions in the classroom to cultivate creativity and cognitive abilities and improve students’ LP. To build AI-based capabilities among students, the training and development of educators in AI-based areas is paramount (Sharma et al., 2024). Hence, we suggest that the manage- ment of educational institutions frequently organize faculty develop- ment programs to build AI capabilities among students. Moreover, educational institutions can collaborate with AI-based organizations to enhance academia-industry connections and include experts from the industry on their boards to get expert guidance on integrating AI-based 

technologies into their curricula. Furthermore, the study has practical implications for policymakers as well. Policymakers worldwide must recognize the growing demand for a skilled workforce and make it mandatory for educational in- stitutions to make AI an integral part of their curriculum across diverse domains. We suggest policymakers set up AI labs in educational in- stitutions with modern infrastructure and experts, which educational institutions can use to train the faculty and students on applying AI- based technologies. Moreover, policymakers can work in a public- private partnership model to provide the necessary infrastructure related to modern technologies to educational institutions. Furthermore, we suggest that the Indian government prioritize building AIC among students through collaboration with leading global technological com- panies to bring the latest and state-of-the-art knowledge to Indian educational institutions. Notably, integrating AI in education and building AI-based capabilities among students enhances students’ LP. Hence, educators must ensure the balanced utilization of AI-based re- sources and human-based pedagogical interventions. For instance, AI- based resources can be utilized for assessment and personalized learning; however, human intervention is required for emotional sup- port, mentorship, and the development of critical thinking. Moreover, we suggest conducting faculty development programs that emphasize the blended pedagogy encompassing human and technological in- terventions. In addition, while utilizing AI in education, algorithmic bias, student privacy issues, and overdependence on technology may result in unintended consequences, such as less human interaction and an elevation in existing inequalities in education. To address these un- intended consequences, educational institutions must develop inclusive AI policies and establish transparent governance procedures. These policy interventions can build AI-based capabilities among students, significantly enhancing their cognitive abilities, confidence, and learning performance. Building AIC among students not only enhances their LP but also creates a future-ready workforce, brings technological advancements through innovation, and achieves economic and sus- tainable growth crucial for building knowledge-based societies.

## 7. Conclusion, limitations and future research avenues

The discussion among educators, researchers, and policymakers on the role of AI-based technologies in shaping the academic landscape has risen substantially over the last few years (Mikalef and Gupta, 2021). Integrating AI in higher education is vital in developing future-ready skills required to handle the modern complexities in the current work- ing environment ([Celik et al., 2024)](#shaping-the-lp-of-children-at-the-school-level-third-the-present-study-bandura-a-freeman-wh-lightsey-r-1999-self-efficacy-the-exercise-of-control-utilizes-a-survey-questionnaire-to-gather-data-from-the-respondents-j-cogn-psychother-13-2-158166-httpsdoiorg1018910889-). Therefore, the present study ex- amines how AIC impacts LP with the mediating effect of CC, SE, CR, and SLC. The present study identified that all five variables in the study have a significant impact on LP, with SLC having the most significant impact on LP, followed by CC, AIC, SE, and CR, respectively. Moreover, the current study reveals that CC, SE, CR, and SLC establish a complemen- tary partial mediation between AIC and LP. The study outcomes reveal that AIC is a significant phenomenon to consider in higher education, when combined with other factors such as CC, SE, CR, and SLC, pro- foundly influencing students’ LP.

Although the research contributes significantly to the literature and has practical implications for diverse stakeholders, it has certain draw- backs. First, the study presents the findings by including AIC predictors and CC, SE, CR, and SLC as mediators. Hence, the researchers in the future can include other predictors, such as the availability of technol- ogy and technical proficiency to predict the students’ LP. Moreover, researchers can examine the influence of moderators, such as de- mographic variables, ethics, trust, and motivation, on the relationship between AIC and LP to enrich the literature. Second, the study examines the influence of AIC on LP in the presence of CC, SE, CR, and SLC on students’ LP only. Future scholars can conduct studies on how AIC can influence the teaching and research performance of educators in higher education. Moreover, researchers can examine the role of AI adoption in
